name: The Fateshaper
body:
Fateshapers are divine casters, devoted to the notion of time and chance as the greatest powers in the universe. All things rise and fall with time and circumstance. Fateshapers seek to become intrinsically linked to these concepts and powers so deeply that they manifest dominion over them.

Role: The fateshaper is a single target debuffer and party buffer. It focuses on rerolls both for enemies and allies.

Alignment: Any.

Hit Die: d8

Starting Wealth: 4d4 x 10 (100 gp). In addition, each character begins play with an outfit worth 10 gp or less.

Class Skills

The martial master’s class skills are: Appraise (Int), Bluff (Cha), Craft (Int), Diplomacy (Cha), Heal (Wis), Knowledge (arcana) (Int), Knowledge (history) (Int), Knowledge (planes) (Int), Knowledge (religion) (Int), Linguistics (Int), Perception (Wis), Perform (Cha), Profession (Wis), Sense Motive (Wis), Spellcraft (Int), and Use Magic Device (Cha).

Skill Ranks per Level: 4 + Int modifier

Class Features

The following are the class features of the fateshaper.

Weapon and Armor Proficiency

All simple weapons plus the scythe, shortsword, starknife, and whip. Fateshapers also gain proficiency in light armor.

Spellcasting

A fateshaper casts divine spells which are drawn from the fateshaper spell list. A fateshaper does not prepare spells in advance, instead a fateshaper may cast any spell on the fateshaper spell list using their available spell slots.

To cast a spell, a fateshaper must have a Wisdom score equal to at least 10 + the spell level. The Difficulty Class for a saving throw against a fateshaper’s spell is 10 + the spell level + the fateshaper’s Wisdom modifier.

Like other spellcasters, a fateshaper can cast only a certain number of spells of each spell level per day.

The base daily spell allotment is given on Table 1-2: Fateshaper Spells per Day. In addition, a fateshaper receives bonus spells per day if they have a high Wisdom score.

Orisons: Fateshapers can cast a number of orisons, or 0-level spells, each day. At the start of each day the fateshaper chooses a number of orisons to have available that day. The number of different orisons the fateshaper may have available each day is listed on the Table 1-2: Fateshaper Spells per Day under 0th level spells. Unlike other spells, orisons are not expended when cast and may be cast again.

Predictions (Su)

Starting at 1st level, when the fateshaper regains their spells they also gain a pool of power called Predictions. This represents minor divinations, rituals, and omens the fateshaper has performed recently and can impact the world around them. This pool is equal to the fateshaper’s Wisdom modifier + an additional Prediction for every 4 class levels.

Bolster Fate (Su)

At 1st level, by pulling at the fabric of existence a fateshaper can influence the outcome of events nearby. Whenever an ally within 30 feet of the fateshaper (or the fateshaper themself) would fail an attack roll, saving throw, or skill check the fateshaper may spend a Prediction as an immediate action to have that player roll again, the target may choose to use either roll. At 3rd level, this reroll is made with an additional +2 insight bonus, this bonus increases by an additional +2 at 8th, 12th and 17th levels to a maximum of +8.

Chronomancy (Su)

Fateshapers have learned to make time work for them in regards to magic. At 2nd level, by spending one round casting any spell on the fatesaper spell list, with a casting time of less than one round, the fateshaper can choose one of the following:

Increase the range of that spell by one step (from touch to close, close to medium, or medium to long)
Gain a +2 insight bonus on any attack rolls associated with the spell being cast
Increase the save DC of the spell by +1.
Improved Counterspell (Su)

Fateshapers learn to dismiss the magic of others as an extension of their growing mastery over fate and chance. At 4th level, a fateshaper gains Improved Counterspell as a bonus feat.

Harbinger (Su)

The passage of a fateshaper alters the fabric of time in small but noticeable ways. At 5th level, when rolling for initiative the fateshaper and all allies within 10 feet gain the fateshaper’s bolster fate bonus to the initiative roll. In addition, the fateshaper may spend a Prediction whenever they roll initiative and have a creature of their choice roll twice. The fateshaper decides if the target uses the lower or higher of the two rolls.

Doomed Portent (Su)

Fateshapers eventually learn not only to tip fate in their favor, but also to manipulate it against their foes directly. At 6th level, the fateshaper may now spend a Prediction as an immediate action to target a creature with no more than twice as many HD as their own character level and force it to reroll a successful attack roll. The target takes a penalty on the new roll equal to the fateshaper’s bolster fate bonus, if the new attack roll misses then negate all effects of the previous attack.

A Stitch In Time (Su)

At 7th level, fateshapers gain more of an understanding of time manipulation. When using their chronomancy ability the fateshaper may now choose two options if they both apply to the spell being cast.

Superior Counterspell (Su)

After many battles and a growing understanding of how magic shapes the world, the fateshaper becomes even more adept at countermagic. At 9th level, a fateshaper now only needs to expend a spell of the same level or higher to counter a spell rather than the same spell or a spell of the same school.

Stretch Time (Su)

Fateshapers learn that every moment counts, and they intend to have as many moments as possible. At 10th level, the fateshaper gains the ability to spend two predictions to cast haste as a spell-like ability with a caster level equal to their character level.

Practiced Fortune Teller (Su)

At 10th level the fateshaper’s number of Predictions per day increases to 1/2 their class level + their Wisdom modifier. Additionally the fateshaper may now use bolster fate once per round as a free action that may be used outside of their turn.

Utterly Predictable (Su)

After thousands of hours reading the world around them, fateshapers begin to understand the flow of time very intimately. At 11th level, a fateshaper treats any roll of lower than 10 on initiative as a 10. In addition, by spending a Prediction when rolling for initiative the fateshaper can cause all other creatures in a 30 feet radius to be treated as though they rolled a 10 on initiative rather than actually rolling.

Sudden Misfortune (Su)

At 13th level, the fateshaper’s doomed portent ability may now also force a creature to reroll saving throws.

Perfect Counterspell (Su)

At this stage, a fateshaper truly begins to master magical energy in their reach. At 14th level a fateshaper no longer needs to ready an action to counterspell, instead they may spend 2 Predictions as an immediate action to attempt a counterspell.

Alter Destiny (Su)

A fateshaper eventually grows so powerful that they begin to have sway over when a creature’s final moments arrive. At 15th level, whenever the fateshaper or an ally within 60 feet would drop to 0 or fewer hit points, or be slain outright, the fateshaper may spend 3 Predictions as an immediate action to treat that creature as though it was unaffected by whatever damage or effect would have slain them, leaving them in the same condition and with the same number of hit points as they were before that action.

Portentous Wave (Su)

At 16th level, the fateshaper may spend 2 Predictions as a standard action and cause their doomed portent ability to affect the next d20 roll all enemies within 60 feet of the fateshaper would make before the fateshaper’s next turn.

As Foretold (Su)

Fateshapers claim dominion over what might be, just as much as what is. At 18th level, whenever a fateshaper would cast, or be affected by, a spell which uses a table of results to determine its effect the fateshaper may choose the result. In addition the fateshaper no longer suffers a failure chance on spells such as teleport or augury.

Master of Fate (Su)

At 20th level, a fateshaper reaches the pinnacle of their dominion over time and fate. By spending 4 Predictions, a fateshaper of this level can cast maximized time stop as a spell-like ability. When the time stop spell-like ability is used, the fateshaper may spend additional Predictions to allow other creatures to also act during it. The allies must still follow all the normal restrictions on actions they are allowed to take. Each creature beyond the fateshaper to be affected requires the spending of 2 Predictions. In addition the fateshaper may act during a time stop cast by another creature.
